questions.q: What is the core idea behind PageRank?
options: PageRank only works on graphs with fewer than 100 nodes
A node's importance is simply the number of properties it has
PageRank ranks nodes purely alphabetically by name
A node is important if it's linked to by other important nodes — importance flows recursively through the graph until scores converge
questions.explain: PageRank's defining idea, originally built for ranking web pages, is that importance flows recursively from being linked to by other important nodes.

options: The physical storage size of a node on disk
The total number of properties stored on a node
How often a node sits on the shortest path between other pairs of nodes — identifying bridges in the graph
How many labels a node has
questions.explain: A node with high betweenness is a bridge that many shortest paths must pass through, regardless of how many direct connections it has itself.

questions.q: Why can a node have very few direct connections but still score extremely high on betweenness centrality?
options: This situation is impossible — betweenness always correlates with degree
High betweenness only happens on nodes with zero relationships
Because it can be the sole bridge connecting two otherwise-separate parts of the graph, so many shortest paths are forced to pass through it
Betweenness centrality is unrelated to a node's position in the graph
questions.explain: The lesson gives the example of the one person connecting engineering and sales — few direct connections, but a critical bridge role.

questions.q: What makes degree centrality the cheapest centrality measure to compute?
options: It's just a count of a node's direct relationships, requiring no traversal or iteration across the graph
It uses machine learning models, which run faster than traditional algorithms
It requires building a full graph projection with all algorithms enabled
It only works after PageRank has already been computed
questions.explain: Degree centrality is a simple relationship count with no iterative traversal needed, unlike PageRank or betweenness.

questions.q: Which of these is named in the lesson as a real use case for centrality algorithms?
options: Identifying the most influential accounts in a social graph or finding single points of failure in a network
Enforcing referential integrity via foreign keys
Normalizing a relational schema to third normal form
Encrypting a database connection string
questions.explain: The lesson names influence ranking and identifying key/bridge nodes (single points of failure) as real centrality use cases.
